frontMatter.objective:
Objectives:

1. Standardization: To establish uniform procedures across all operations, ensuring consistency and quality in service delivery.
2. Efficiency: To streamline workflows, reduce redundancies, and enhance operational efficiency.
3. Compliance: To ensure adherence to legal, regulatory, and industry standards in all aspects of our operations.
4. Customer Satisfaction: To enhance the customer experience through reliable, timely, and personalized services.
5. Innovation: To foster a culture of continuous improvement and innovation in our service offerings and internal processes.
6. Sustainability: To integrate environmentally and socially responsible practices into our operations, contributing to sustainable development goals.

blocks.text: This SOP documents the procedures already adopted and in active practice to manage waste generation, segregation, safe disposal, and compliance tracking across our pan-India operations.

All employees, vendors, and housekeeping teams are trained and actively following this SOP as part of our commitment to environmental stewardship and regulatory compliance. Our waste management policy reflects our organizational value of sustainability and aligns with national waste legislation as well as our internal ESG goals.
This SOP applies to all employees, contractors, and housekeeping staff at all office locations of Riya Travel and Tours (India) Pvt Ltd (Group).

responsibilities: Ensure implementation of the waste management process, vendor coordination, and awareness training.
Follow segregation and disposal protocols.
Dispose of waste responsibly in designated bins and comply with awareness practices.

rows.definition: Organic waste like food scraps, tea bags, etc.
Discarded electronic items like old cables, batteries, keyboards.

body.text: Each office has been equipped with a 4-bin segregation system at all major points including workstations, pantry, washrooms, and receptions:

Green Bins: Biodegradable (food waste, tissues)
Blue Bins: Recyclables (paper, bottles, dry plastic)
Red Bins: Sanitary Waste (napkins, masks)
White Lockbox: E-Waste (cables, cartridges, batteries)

Signage in English and local languages is placed above each bin. Posters with illustrations are updated every 6 months. These posters also include QR codes that link to internal awareness videos and FAQs for new joiners. Waste sorting guides are laminated and placed on employee noticeboards for easy reference.
We ensure that all bins are made of recyclable materials and are replaced every 18 months as part of the sustainability replacement cycle.
Waste is collected twice a day (10:30 AM and 5:30 PM) by trained in-house housekeeping staff.
Each collection is documented in the Daily Waste Collection Logbook, maintained digitally at the reception desk and synchronized weekly with the central server.

Waste is transported using covered trolleys, marked and dedicated to each waste category. These trolleys are color-coded and labeled to avoid cross-contamination. Housekeeping staff wear high-visibility vests while transporting the waste to ensure safety during movement through office corridors.

Central storage rooms (present at each office floor) are locked and cleaned daily after the evening round. These rooms have separate shelving for e-waste and sanitary disposal packets, and are equipped with fire retardant bins as per fire safety guidelines.
We are partnered with EcoGreen Disposal Pvt Ltd and RecycleIndia Services, both registered with the CPCB and local municipalities.
Pickups are scheduled as follows:

Dry Recyclables: Every Tuesday and Friday
Wet/Biodegradable Waste: Daily
E-Waste: Once every quarter
Sanitary Waste: Twice a week via specialized collection

All vendors undergo a yearly review of compliance documentation, licenses, and disposal processes. Disposal Certificates (Form 3) and vendor manifests are stored in our Compliance Drive (Admin > ESG > Waste Records) and hard copies filed at HO Admin.
We also maintain an Annual Vendor Performance Summary that tracks punctuality, compliance incidents, and waste tonnage picked per quarter.
As part of our “Go Paperless” campaign initiated in July 2023, printing has reduced by 60%. Digital approvals, e-invoicing, and online itineraries have been adopted as default practices.
Confidential papers are shredded using two high-capacity shredders installed at HO and zonal offices. These shredders are maintained quarterly and covered under an AMC (Annual Maintenance Contract).

Shredded material is picked up monthly by our paper recycling partner and logged via the Shredding Log Sheet (Form-PR/07). All shredded paper is weighed and recorded as part of our office sustainability KPIs.
Dedicated white e-waste boxes with tamper-proof locks are installed in IT rooms and Admin blocks.
Our staff from the IT and Admin teams manually log each deposited item in the E-Waste Register (EW-Log-22), including serial number, disposal reason, and asset tag (if applicable).

Quarterly pickups are documented with disposal certificates and serial number tracking sheets, which are also verified by our internal audit team annually. In FY 2024–25, we safely disposed of 183 kg of e-waste across all zones.

Riya Travel and Tours (India) Pvt Ltd has institutionalized a robust program to actively reduce internal waste generation through systematic reuse, recovery, and repurposing initiatives. This proactive approach has significantly minimized landfill contributions and enhanced resource efficiency across all operations.

All single-use plastics, including disposable cutlery, cups, and packaging materials, have been completely phased out from pantries and replaced with durable stainless-steel alternatives and certified compostable items sourced from approved sustainable vendors. This transition is monitored quarterly to ensure zero plastic usage compliance.
Shipping and transit boxes received through logistics operations are rigorously collected, inspected, and catalogued for multiple reuse cycles within inter-office dispatches. Over 85% of packaging needs are met through this internal reuse program, reducing dependency on new materials.
Damaged or obsolete office furniture components are systematically refurbished in partnership with certified local craftsmen. Refurbishment protocols extend the functional lifespan of desks, chairs, and storage units by an average of 3 years, effectively lowering waste generation and procurement costs.
Confidential shredded paper, beyond secure destruction, is repurposed as cushioning material in outbound shipments and internal packaging, diverting several tons of waste from landfill annually.
Outdated event banners, marketing materials, and promotional fabrics are collected and repurposed by partnered vendors into reusable bags, mats, and other functional items, exemplifying circular economy principles in action.
Riya Travel and Tours continuously pursues operational excellence by optimizing material consumption, integrating best practices and cutting-edge technologies into everyday workflows.

All office printers and copiers are configured by default to duplex printing and grayscale output, significantly reducing paper use without compromising document clarity.
Employee onboarding, internal communications, and document approvals have transitioned fully to digital platforms, supported by electronic signatures and cloud-based collaboration tools, eliminating unnecessary physical copies.
Centralized issuance of stationery and office supplies controls inventory levels, prevents overstocking, and curtails wastage through usage tracking and monthly reconciliation.
Courier and mail packaging primarily utilize reusable folders and eco-certified materials, with a centralized system tracking return and reuse rates to maximize lifecycle.
Commitment to sustainability is embedded in Riya Travel and Tours’ procurement strategy, mandating the preferential use of eco-friendly and bio-based input materials to minimize environmental impact.

All cleaning agents and consumables are herbal, biodegradable, and certified by the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB), ensuring safe disposal and reduced chemical hazards.
Compostable garbage bags are standardized across all sites, complying with Indian biodegradability standards and enhancing organic waste processing.
Stationery products, including paper, notebooks, and promotional items, are sourced from vendors specializing in recycled content and seed-based inks, supporting circular economy models.
Toner cartridges and printer consumables follow refillable and buyback programs in partnership with original equipment manufacturers (OEMs), significantly cutting e-waste generation.
Vendor sustainability certifications such as ISO 14001 and Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) compliance are mandatory prerequisites, with procurement teams regularly auditing supplier adherence.
Beyond the foundational four-bin segregation, Riya Travel and Tours has established a comprehensive multi-stream waste sorting framework tailored to meet regulatory and operational demands.

Waste is systematically sorted into six distinct streams: paper, glass, metals, plastics, organic/biodegradable waste, and hazardous/sanitary waste, ensuring precise handling and maximized recycling recovery.

Dedicated receptacles for glass and metal waste have been installed at strategic points in all major offices, complemented by frequent employee training to reinforce compliance and correct disposal practices.

The Segregation Handling Manual (SHM-2024), updated annually, governs sorting standards and procedures. All employees, housekeeping, and vendor teams are regularly assessed on their adherence to these protocols during monthly audits.

Waste disposal strictly conforms to local municipal guidelines and CPCB mandates, with hazardous and sanitary waste handled through licensed vendors using environmentally sound methods such as incineration or secure landfill.
This detailed stream-based sorting ensures maximum diversion from landfill, achieving over 78% recycling rates year-on-year across locations.
The following table summarizes the main waste streams, the typical sources of waste generation within our operations, and the corresponding disposal methods employed:

rows: Office documents, printing, packaging, shredded confidential documents
Collected for recycling via certified paper recyclers
Beverage bottles, pantry waste, broken office glass
Collected in dedicated bins; sent for recycling to authorized facilities
Stationery supplies, office maintenance (e.g., clips, wires), packaging
Sorted in metal bins; handed over to licensed metal scrap recyclers
Packaging, food containers, plastic cutlery (phased out gradually)
Segregated and sent to registered plastic recyclers
Food waste, plant-based materials from pantry and cafeteria
Collected daily; processed through composting vendors or bio-digesters
Masks, napkins, sanitary pads, medical waste from first aid
Collected separately; disposed through licensed hazardous waste handlers via incineration or secure landfill

body.text: Our IT department leads in reducing electronic waste through a rigorous refurbishment and redeployment program, promoting asset longevity and operational cost-efficiency.

Hardware refurbishment involves detailed disassembly, thorough cleaning, comprehensive functional testing, component upgrades, and final certification before redeployment.
Refurbished equipment primarily supports training labs, reception areas, and temporary or contract staff, ensuring high utilization of existing assets and reducing new procurement demand.
All refurbishment activities and asset movements are meticulously recorded in the Asset Refurbishment Sheet (Form-IT/Refurb-05) and updated in the centralized inventory management system.
During FY 2024-25, 41 laptops and 16 desktops were successfully refurbished and redeployed, reflecting a 25% increase in reuse compared to the previous year.
Continuous improvement is driven through feedback loops involving IT support, end-users, and sustainability teams.
Riya Travel and Tours upholds the highest standards of health and safety in all waste management activities.

Housekeeping staff are provided with and consistently use Personal Protective Equipment (PPE), including gloves, masks, and aprons, rigorously tracked through the Monthly PPE Log (PPE-Log-02).
Bins, collection trolleys, and storage areas undergo daily sanitation using eco-friendly, herbal disinfectants, verified by cleaning supervisors through checklist compliance.
Spillage incidents and related hazards are promptly addressed, with incidents logged and resolved within 15 minutes under the Rapid Response Protocol (RRP-2024/01) to maintain a safe and hygienic environment.
Regular health and safety briefings reinforce safe waste handling and emergency preparedness among all staff.

narrative.text: Continuous monitoring, systematic auditing, and data-driven improvement are pillars of our waste management program.

Monthly waste audits are performed using the comprehensive Waste Management Audit Checklist (WM-AuditForm-03), examining segregation accuracy, collection timeliness, vendor compliance, and hygiene standards.
Audit findings are thoroughly reviewed at quarterly ESG Committee meetings, where corrective actions and innovations are prioritized and scheduled.
Performance metrics, audit data, and employee feedback inform annual SOP revisions, ensuring Riya Travel and Tours maintains a best-in-class waste management system aligned with evolving regulations and sustainability goals.

sections.title: Employee Exchange Portal for Office Supplies and Equipment

blocks.text: Riya Travel and Tours has successfully implemented a centralized digital portal, “Riya Reuse Connect,” designed to facilitate the internal exchange of surplus or unused office supplies and equipment among employees across all departments and units. This initiative is a key component of our waste reduction and resource optimization strategy, underscoring our commitment to sustainable and responsible business practices.

Through Riya Reuse Connect, employees can list items such as stationery, furniture components, IT peripherals, and other reusable assets. Colleagues can browse, request, and receive these items easily, enabling efficient redistribution and extending the lifecycle of company resources while reducing unnecessary procurement and waste generation.

The portal incorporates structured approval workflows, asset tracking, and detailed reporting to ensure accountability, transparency, and smooth operations. This system enables management to monitor reuse trends, identify high-demand items, and make data-driven decisions to further enhance resource utilization.

Ongoing training sessions, periodic communications, and awareness campaigns actively encourage participation, ensuring that all employees are familiar with the portal’s features and benefits. By fostering a culture of sharing and reuse, Riya Reuse Connect not only minimizes waste but also promotes interdepartmental collaboration and cost savings.

The portal has already demonstrated measurable impacts by reducing procurement expenses, decreasing landfill contributions, and strengthening our organization’s environmental responsibility credentials. Moving forward, the platform will continue to evolve with user feedback and technological enhancements to further support our sustainability goals.

This SOP establishes operational framework for responsible water management. We are committed to minimizing water consumption across our office infrastructure and partner services, while promoting efficient and sustainable practices among employees, customers, and vendors.

This SOP applies to all corporate offices, branch locations, travel-related events, and external service partners involved in hospitality, catering, and destination management where RIYA GROUP exercises operational control or influence.

responsibilities: Accountable for defining water-saving targets and ensuring alignment with the Group's broader sustainability strategy.
Implements and maintains water-efficient systems across locations and monitors consumption trends.
Ensures that all service contracts include clauses on water efficiency and sustainability requirements.
Oversee employee engagement programs and water-related awareness campaigns.
Ensures that travel, hotel, and event partners maintain water-conscious operations in alignment with our standards.

body.text: All offices are equipped with water-efficient systems including:

Low-flow taps and aerators
Dual-flush toilets
Push-tap or sensor-based faucets in common areas
New fixtures must meet water efficiency certification standards (e.g., BIS or equivalent).
Facilities teams conduct monthly plumbing inspections.
Any leakages reported by staff or found during checks are repaired within 48 hours.
Maintenance logs are maintained digitally with time-stamped updates for accountability.
Smart water meters are installed in all large offices; manual meter readings are done weekly in smaller branches.
Monthly consumption reports are generated and reviewed by the ESG Manager to identify spikes or inefficiencies.
Branches exceeding baseline usage thresholds are supported with corrective action plans.
Water-saving signage is installed in:

Pantry/kitchen areas
Restrooms
Utility zones (if any)
Employees are trained at induction and via quarterly refreshers on responsible water use practices such as:

Turning off taps after use
Reporting drips or leaks immediately
Avoiding unnecessary use of water during cleaning
Cleaning teams use water-efficient techniques such as:

Mopping with minimal water
Using spray bottles instead of open buckets for surface cleaning
No use of running water for washing floors or outdoor spaces
RO systems (if installed) are maintained to minimize water rejection and wastewater is reused (e.g., for mopping or toilet flushing where feasible).

narrative.text:
Facilities Manager submits a quarterly water audit report to the ESG Manager.
ESG Team conducts spot audits twice a year to verify compliance across locations.
Non-compliance is addressed through written notices and retraining of facility or housekeeping staff.

blocks.text: To establish systematic practices for managing and reducing energy consumption across all office operations of RIYA TRAVEL AND TOURS (INDIA) PVT LTD (GROUP), thereby contributing to climate action, operational efficiency, and sustainability objectives.

This SOP applies to all offices, departments, employees, and service providers under the RIYA Group, with specific focus on lighting systems, HVAC systems, IT infrastructure, office equipment, and employee engagement related to energy conservation.

rows.definition: Coordinated activities to monitor, control, and reduce energy use.
Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning systems.
Internal team responsible for environmental, social, and governance practices.
Use of advanced devices to monitor energy consumption in real time.

responsibilities: Oversight of implementation, monitoring, reporting, and improvement of energy management practices.
Execution of energy-efficient infrastructure and equipment installations and maintenance.
Organizing training programs on energy conservation.
Adherence to energy-saving guidelines and participation in relevant training.
Compliance with company's energy and sustainability procurement criteria.

body.text: Smart energy meters and sub-metering systems are installed across office floors to enable precise tracking of energy consumption in real time. Collected data is analyzed monthly by the ESG team using customized dashboards that flag abnormal consumption patterns or system inefficiencies. These insights are used to inform decisions related to retrofitting, maintenance, or operational adjustments. Summary reports are shared with leadership on a quarterly basis to ensure alignment with corporate sustainability goals and continuous improvement.

All company-operated offices have been upgraded to 100% energy-efficient LED lighting systems, following a structured replacement roadmap. Motion sensors and dimming technologies are installed in meeting rooms, restrooms, corridors, and low-traffic zones to automatically optimize lighting use based on occupancy. Office layouts are strategically planned to maximize exposure to natural daylight, which not only reduces dependency on artificial lighting but also improves employee well-being and productivity. Routine inspections are carried out quarterly to assess lighting performance and detect early signs of inefficiency, with findings documented and corrective measures initiated within the same review cycle.

Energy-efficient HVAC systems, including central air conditioners and high-performance heat pumps, have been deployed in all locations, replacing legacy systems that failed to meet current efficiency benchmarks. Each HVAC unit is connected to smart controls featuring occupancy sensors, temperature automation, and variable speed drives to allow real-time responsiveness to environmental and usage conditions. The engineering and facilities team conducts monthly preventive maintenance, ensuring air filters, compressors, and duct systems are cleaned, calibrated, and functioning at optimal load capacity. All maintenance records are logged digitally and reviewed during monthly ESG committee meetings, with performance metrics benchmarked against historical energy usage data.

All office equipment, including printers, copiers, projectors, and kitchen appliances, is procured based on energy efficiency ratings, with preference given to BEE 5-Star and ENERGY STAR-certified models. Default settings for all devices are configured to energy-saving modes, including auto-sleep and power-down functions after periods of inactivity. Employees are trained to use shared devices efficiently and encouraged to shut down equipment at the end of each workday. Routine audits are conducted by the administration team to ensure compliance with energy-saving protocols and identify outdated equipment for phased replacement.

The company's server rooms and IT infrastructure are equipped with energy-efficient processors, power supplies, and precision air-cooling systems designed to significantly reduce energy use. Virtualization of servers and cloud migration of services have been implemented to reduce the physical hardware footprint and related cooling demands. Energy usage of IT systems is monitored in real-time through power usage effectiveness (PUE) indicators, with analytics reviewed quarterly by the ESG team to identify trends and opportunities for further optimization. In addition, employee computers are pre-configured with automatic power-saving settings, and periodic awareness campaigns promote responsible digital behavior to further curb unnecessary energy consumption.

The company's procurement policy prioritizes the purchase of energy-efficient products and services, extending to lighting, HVAC components, IT equipment, and appliances. All vendors and service providers are evaluated on their energy and environmental credentials during the onboarding process. Contracts include clauses that mandate compliance with the company's energy management guidelines, and periodic reviews are conducted to ensure ongoing alignment. Through this approach, the company ensures that its supply chain supports its broader energy reduction objectives.

All employees are required to complete comprehensive, mandatory training programs focused on energy conservation and climate action. These training sessions are tailored to help staff understand how their daily actions directly contribute to energy reduction and climate goals, making it clear that sustainability is a shared responsibility across all departments. Training materials include step-by-step guidelines, internal case studies, and best practices related to reducing energy usage and GHG emissions. Completion of these trainings is strictly tracked by the ESG team via an internal Learning Management System (LMS), with training records, certificates, and refresher logs maintained for internal audits and external disclosures.

sops.title: External Feedback on Health and Safety

blocks.text: At RIYA TRAVEL AND TOURS (INDIA) PVT LTD (GROUP), we recognize that valuable insights into our health and safety practices often come from those outside our organization. This SOP outlines the structured approach for receiving, documenting, analyzing, and responding to external feedback on health and safety matters from clients, authorities, community stakeholders, and visitors to our office locations. The aim is to foster a safe, compliant, and continuously improving workplace environment.

This SOP applies to all branches, departments, and employees of RIYA TRAVEL AND TOURS (INDIA) PVT LTD (GROUP). It encompasses all external health and safety feedback mechanisms, including emails, calls, surveys, online forms, regulatory notices, and in-person interactions.

responsibilities: The CEO is responsible for providing strategic oversight of the external feedback process, approving updates to this SOP, allocating necessary resources for its implementation, and reviewing the overall performance of health and safety improvements initiated through external inputs.

The Director ensures that external feedback is systematically reviewed and integrated into the company's health and safety practices. They are also responsible for tracking resolution progress and coordinating with relevant teams to implement corrective actions.

The Executive Director manages all external communications related to health and safety feedback, including responding to regulatory authorities and community stakeholders. They ensure that all communications are professional, transparent, and confidential.

Regional Heads are responsible for implementing feedback-driven health and safety improvements across the branches under their jurisdiction. They ensure that all required changes are communicated clearly to their teams and executed on time.

The HR & Admin Manager coordinates the handling of external feedback within the organization. This includes organizing employee training sessions, maintaining accurate records, and ensuring that reported issues are followed up until resolution.

The Health & Safety Officer serves as the primary reviewer of all external feedback received. They are responsible for assessing the urgency and severity of each issue, initiating investigations, and collaborating with other departments to determine appropriate corrective measures.

The IT & Facilities Team addresses safety concerns related to infrastructure, such as lighting, ergonomic setups, or ventilation in office premises. They are responsible for scheduling timely maintenance and ensuring that all facility-related hazards are resolved efficiently.

body.text: External parties may submit feedback through the following:
Multiple options are available—email, website, hotline, or social media. All entries are routed to the Health & Safety Officer within 24 hours.
All feedback is treated with the highest level of confidentiality. Anonymity is respected upon request.

Acknowledgment: Within 24 hours
Initial Review: Within 48 hours
Resolution: Based on severity (typically within 3–10 working days)

All feedback is recorded in the External Feedback Register (EFR), a secure digital database.
Each entry includes date, source, issue summary, severity, location, response actions, and resolution.
A Unique Tracking Number is generated for monitoring.
Access is restricted to authorized health and safety personnel.

48-Hour Review Window: The Health & Safety Officer evaluates all new entries.
Classification:
Urgent: Requires immediate response (e.g., hazard in a public area).
Non-Urgent: Tracked, reviewed, and resolved as per timeline.
Prioritization: Based on potential impact, reputational risk, and legal implications.

A. Urgent Issues
Assemble cross-functional team (HR, Facilities, Security).
Take immediate steps: e.g., restrict access, provide medical attention, repair malfunctioning equipment.
Prepare an incident report within 48 hours.
Communicate with the feedback provider with transparency.
B. Non-Urgent Issues
Assign department head to lead investigation.
Develop a Corrective Action Plan (CAP) with tasks, timelines, and accountability.
Keep the feedback provider updated until closure.
Conduct a post-resolution evaluation.

rows: Conducted by the HSE Officer and Admin team using logs, issue trackers, and feedback analysis.
HSE committee prepares a consolidated report highlighting patterns, resolution efficiency, and stakeholder feedback.
Leadership reviews overall effectiveness of the system and updates the SOP accordingly.

blocks.text: RIYA TRAVEL AND TOURS conducts stakeholder workshops, townhalls, and feedback analysis sessions annually. Findings are used to update training modules, redesign office safety features, and modify emergency protocols. Improvements are recorded and tracked in the Health & Safety Management System.

All feedback-related actions comply with applicable Indian labor, health, and safety regulations. The company benchmarks its practices against ISO 45001 and other international standards wherever feasible.

sops.title: Sustainability Customer Offerings and Environmental Initiatives

blocks.text: This SOP outlines RIYA TRAVEL AND TOURS (INDIA) PVT LTD (GROUP)'s approach to empowering customers with sustainable travel options. It consolidates our offerings in carbon footprint education, plant-based catering, reduction of single-use plastics, electric vehicle access, alternative transport promotion, and biodiversity-conscious tour planning.
Applies to all customer-facing services and packages including corporate travel, retail bookings, event planning, catering services, and transportation.

responsibilities: Oversee design and implementation of all sustainability programs.
Ensure visibility of offerings and customer support integration.
Create awareness through brochures, signage, digital content, and campaigns.
Coordinate execution of initiatives across services and tours.
Onboard and audit vendors for compliance with plant-based, electric vehicle, and reusable product standards.

steps.heading: Carbon Footprint Calculation Programs and Customer Support
Provision of Plant-Based Food and Beverage Options
Actions to Replace Single-Use Plastics with Reusable Containers
Offer of Electric-Powered Vehicles (EVs) for Transportation Services
Promotion of Alternative Modes of Transportation Over Private Vehicles
Energy Efficiency in Office and Service Operations
Consideration of Nature Impacts During Tours
Community Engagement and Support for Local Sustainability Projects

narrative.text:
The ESG Manager shall establish performance indicators to monitor implementation of each initiative and ensure alignment with the company’s environmental goals.
Periodic internal audits will be conducted across departments and partner operations to assess compliance with sustainability standards.
Non-compliance cases shall trigger immediate corrective action plans and follow-up reviews to ensure timely resolution.
Vendor contracts will include sustainability clauses, and vendors will undergo compliance checks based on agreed KPIs related to emissions, waste, and material use.

blocks.text: Riya Group of Companies and its Affiliates/Subsidiaries are committed to upholding a fair, transparent, and non-discriminatory recruitment process. We ensure equal employment opportunities for all individuals, irrespective of caste, creed, religion, gender, sexual orientation, age, disability, marital status, or any other protected characteristic.

We strive to attract and hire the most qualified candidates based on merit, skills, and alignment with our organizational values and needs. Our recruitment practices are designed to foster diversity and inclusion—key pillars of our continued success. All hiring decisions are made solely based on candidates' qualifications and potential, in full compliance with applicable laws and internal policies promoting fairness and equity across our workforce.
This policy ensures that every applicant is treated with dignity and respect, and that no form of bias or favoritism is tolerated at any stage of the hiring process.

body.text: When a job opening becomes available, the hiring manager will work with HR to create a job posting that accurately reflects the duties and requirements of the position. The job posting will include a detailed job description and a list of required qualifications and skills. Talent sourcing platforms used are Job Portals, Placement Agencies, Internal Job Posting, Employee References, Company's career page and social media platforms.

Interested candidates can apply for the position by submitting a resume and cover letter through the company's online application system. It is essential that candidates accurately and thoroughly describe their qualifications and experience in their application materials. Incomplete or inaccurate applications may not be considered.

HR will conduct an initial screening of all candidates to ensure that they meet the minimum requirements for the position. This may include reviewing their resume and cover letter, as well as conducting phone or video interviews. During the initial screening, HR will assess the candidate's qualifications, skills, and fit for the role. Candidates who do not meet the minimum requirements or are not a good fit for the position will not be advanced to the next stage.

Selected candidates shall be invited to participate in an in-person or virtual interview with the hiring manager and/or HR representative. The interview will consist of behavioral and technical questions designed to assess the candidate's fit for the role. It is important that candidates arrive on time and dress appropriately for the interview. During the interview, the candidate can ask questions about the role and the company.

Riya Group is compliant with all the laws, rules and regulations governing employment. Hence, as a documented process before releasing the Offer Letter, the Talent Acquisition / Recruitment Team asks for the documents listed below for verification.

substeps.text: PAN Card - To verify the name and age of the candidate. We as an organization do not entertain and encourage child labour. We only employ candidates who are 18 years or above.
Aadhar Card - To verify the name and address to be used for releasing the offer letter. As this document is a mandate for Universal Account Number / Provident Fund registration.
Salary Slips - To understand the salary break-up of the employee in his current organization.
Bank Statement - To corroborate the salary listed in the salary slips being deposited in the bank account.

body.text: If the candidate is determined to be the best fit for the position, HR will make a job offer in writing. The job offer will include details such as the job title, salary, benefits, and start date. The candidate will have a specified period to accept or decline the offer. If the candidate accepts the offer, they will be required to sign an employment agreement outlining the terms of their employment.

Once the candidate has accepted the job offer and passed the background check, HR will begin the onboarding process. This will include providing information about the company's policies and procedures, as well as setting up the new hire with the necessary tools and resources to succeed in their role. This may include training, onboarding materials, and access to company systems and resources.

Before making a job offer, HR will conduct reference checks with the candidate's previous employers or professional references. This is an essential step in the hiring process, as it allows us to verify the candidate's employment history and gain insight into their work habits and performance.

Before the candidate starts their new job, HR will conduct a background check to verify their education, employment history, and any other relevant information. This may include a criminal background check and verification of the candidate's education and employment history.

blocks.text: Riya Group is, first and foremost, an equal opportunity employer and will never discriminate based on race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. All candidates will be considered for employment based on their qualifications and experience. We are fully committed to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace for all our employees.

Performance management is an ongoing organizational process that aligns individual employee contributions with the company’s strategic objectives. It aims to enhance employee competencies, improve productivity, and support career growth while driving the company’s overall success.

body.text: The Company establishes its annual goals and targets by analyzing market conditions, budget forecasts, and purchase order expectations.
These organizational goals are cascaded down to departmental levels, where specific targets are defined in alignment with company objectives.
Each employee’s individual goals and targets are then set based on their respective department’s priorities and role responsibilities.
The goal-setting process is completed by mid-April each year to ensure clear performance expectations from the start of the appraisal cycle.
Individual goals and targets are formally documented using the designated Goal Setting Form (Form No. 102).

blocks.text: All confirmed employees will be appraised based on their performance at least once in a year. He / She will be given the opportunity to explain their contribution towards the organization and their ability to take more responsibilities.

body.text: Employees are required to complete a self-appraisal honestly and thoughtfully, reflecting on their accomplishments, challenges, and areas for growth. This process encourages self-awareness and prepares employees for meaningful performance discussions with their supervisors.

Supervisors and department heads conduct formal appraisals of their team members at least once annually, evaluating performance against predefined criteria, including Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) and behavioral competencies. Collective bargaining agreements may specify additional guidelines for certain employee groups.
Quantitative measures such as target achievement, efficiency, quality, timeliness, and customer satisfaction.
Qualitative factors including teamwork, communication, initiative, problem-solving, adaptability, and leadership potential.
Performance is rated on a standardized five-point scale — Outstanding, Exceeds Expectations, Meets Expectations, Needs Improvement, and Unsatisfactory.
Ongoing feedback is encouraged throughout the year to support employee development and course correction.
Formal performance discussions occur bi-annually, with an interim review in October and a final appraisal in March.
Employees are given the opportunity to provide comments on their evaluations, fostering open dialogue.
Performance review outcomes are documented in the official appraisal form (Form No. 77).
Based on appraisal results, employees and supervisors jointly create a Career Development Plan (CDP) focused on skill enhancement, career aspirations, and growth opportunities.
The CDP identifies relevant training, mentoring, certifications, and project assignments to support employee development.
The CDP is reviewed at least twice annually to monitor progress and adjust development activities as needed.
All CDPs are maintained by HR to facilitate access to development resources and support.
Successful completion of development objectives positively influences future appraisals and succession planning.

All the confirmed employees are eligible for an annual increment. You cannot claim any increment as a matter of right. This will be at the sole and absolute discretion of the Management and will be based on your performance.

blocks.text: At Riya Group, all employees are guaranteed equal opportunities for promotion, transfer, and role changes, without any discrimination based on gender, age, ethnicity, religion, disability, or any other protected characteristic. Our promotion and mobility practices are designed to be fair, transparent, and based solely on merit, performance, potential, and alignment with organizational needs.

Non-Discrimination in Promotions: Promotions to higher positions are granted on the basis of demonstrated performance, competencies, and readiness to assume greater responsibilities. We strictly prohibit any bias or discriminatory practices in promotional decisions to foster an inclusive and equitable workplace.

All promotion, transfer, and internal job opportunities are communicated transparently through formal channels such as internal job postings, company-wide announcements, and talent marketplace platforms accessible to all eligible employees.
Relevant procedural documents and communication materials explaining the promotion and internal mobility processes are made available to employees to ensure clarity and accessibility.
Riya Group actively promotes internal mobility to support career growth, employee engagement, and organizational flexibility. Our internal mobility initiatives include:

Vertical Mobility: Opportunities for employees to advance to higher levels within the organizational hierarchy through promotions or transfers that reflect increased responsibilities and seniority.
Horizontal Mobility: Facilitation of transfers or role changes within the same job level, allowing employees to gain experience in different functions or departments to broaden skills and knowledge.
Geographical Mobility: Support for employees who choose to take up assignments or roles at different company locations or sites, promoting workforce flexibility and cross-location collaboration.
Transversal Mobility (Cross-Skilling): Encouragement for employees to move across different roles or functions by leveraging transferable skills, enabling cross-functional expertise and career diversification.

The Company maintains documented records of internal job postings, announcements, and the use of internal talent marketplace platforms to track and promote transparency in hiring and role changes.
We implement job shadowing programs, internal mentoring or sponsorship initiatives, and employee job rotation or job swap programs to support skill development and facilitate smooth transitions across roles or departments.
Supervisors and HR partners work closely to identify and recommend suitable internal mobility opportunities aligned with employees’ career aspirations and the organization’s needs.
All internal mobility activities are tracked and reviewed periodically to measure their effectiveness and to continuously improve career development offerings.

By fostering a culture of fair, transparent, and diverse internal mobility, Riya Group ensures employees have multiple pathways for growth, whether through promotion, lateral moves, or expanding their expertise across locations and functions.

blocks.text: This procedure defines the operational practices adopted by RIYA TRAVEL AND TOURS (INDIA) PVT LTD (GROUP) to protect and uphold human rights across all office-based activities. The company maintains a work environment based on dignity, fairness, and legal compliance.
This procedure is applicable to all employees, contract workers, interns, and vendors operating under the administrative control of RIYA GROUP.

responsibilities: Manages the implementation of human rights policies, conducts due diligence during recruitment, and ensures the functioning of grievance mechanisms.
Performs regular assessments and internal audits related to human rights protection, and ensures compliance with applicable national and international frameworks.
Monitor workplace behavior, address potential violations promptly, and submit human rights compliance reports to HR on a quarterly basis.
Operate under strict adherence to the company's code of conduct and are obligated to report any violations confidentially through approved channels.

body.text:
All employment relationships are strictly voluntary and governed by formal employment contracts that are fully compliant with national labor laws and international human rights standards.
Mandatory age verification procedures are applied without exception during onboarding to eliminate any possibility of child labor within company operations.
Under no circumstances are applicants charged recruitment or processing fees, directly or indirectly, by the company or any associated agent.
Human rights orientation is a compulsory component of the induction program for every new employee, with documented acknowledgment of the company's Human Rights Policy.

The company enforces a zero-tolerance policy toward any form of discrimination in recruitment, career advancement, compensation, or workplace behavior.
Decisions related to employment, including hiring, promotions, benefits, and transfers, are exclusively merit-based and role-specific, with strict audit trails.
Any act of bias or discrimination—based on caste, religion, gender, marital status, sexual orientation, age, or disability—is treated as a serious disciplinary offense and investigated under a defined escalation protocol.
Reasonable accommodations are proactively arranged for employees with disabilities, enabling full participation in all work-related functions.

All RIYA office locations are certified for fire safety and occupational health compliance through regular audits by licensed professionals.
Ergonomically designed workspaces, clean drinking water, gender-neutral sanitation facilities, and hygienic conditions are standard across all office locations.
A confidential Employee Assistance Program (EAP) is in place to provide psychological counseling and stress management resources.
The Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) operates with full independence to investigate and resolve complaints related to sexual harassment, with strict adherence to timelines mandated under the POSH Act, 2013.

The company maintains a multi-channel grievance redressal mechanism, allowing complaints via secured email, physical drop boxes, or direct HR reporting without fear of retribution.
All grievances are logged, acknowledged within 3 working days, investigated with due process, and resolved within 10 working days.
Absolute confidentiality is maintained, and complainants are kept informed of progress.
Any retaliation against complainants or whistleblowers triggers immediate disciplinary action, including suspension or termination of the responsible individual(s).

All third-party vendors and partners are contractually obligated to comply with human rights, anti-discrimination, and fair labor practices.
Annual third-party audits are conducted to evaluate supplier practices, including site inspections, document reviews, and worker interviews where applicable.
Vendors found in breach of human rights obligations are immediately placed under corrective action plans, with defined deadlines.
Persistent or serious violations result in termination of business relationships and disqualification from future engagements.

narrative.text: Human rights compliance is monitored through semi-annual audits led by the ESG Manager.
Metrics tracked include grievance resolution rates, harassment case logs, and third-party compliance status.
Summary reports are submitted to top management for review and corrective action, where necessary.

blocks.text: We are committed to safeguarding our confidential data and ensuring the proper retention and disposal of our records. This SOP outlines our guidelines and responsibilities to securely manage sensitive information in compliance with our legal and operational requirements in the travel and tourism industry.

Obtain clear and explicit stakeholder consent for processing, sharing, and retaining confidential travel and customer information.
Protect third-party data including customer travel documents, payment information, and personal details using robust digital (encryption, multi-factor authentication) and physical security measures.
Implement and maintain a detailed records retention schedule that complies with travel industry regulations, tax requirements, and data protection laws.
Ensure transparency by consulting and informing customers about data collection, storage, and sharing practices related to travel bookings and services.
Enforce strict internal controls to restrict unauthorized access to sensitive customer and business data.
Regularly review and update data management practices to adapt to evolving regulations in travel, hospitality, and data protection sectors.
Provide dedicated support channels for customers and partners to address any data-related queries.
Guarantee secure disposal of data once its retention period expires, ensuring compliance with travel industry standards.

This SOP applies to all employees, contractors, and third parties managing our confidential customer travel data, partner information, supplier data, and operational records. It covers both digital and physical records—from collection to secure disposal—across all our office locations, including main facilities and remote work arrangements. Our guidelines ensure compliance with internal policies, travel industry standards, GDPR, Indian IT Act, and regulatory requirements in both routine and emergency scenarios.

responsibilities: Sets overall data strategy and ensures compliance across all operations.
Implements data policies and oversees retention and audit processes.
Manages customer communication, consent, and booking data protection.
Secures reservation data and coordinates with booking platforms.
Handles employee data, consent collection, and privacy training.
Manages financial records and ensures secure payment data handling.
Maintains digital security, backups, and secure data transfers.
Controls access to customer data and manages privacy requests.
Ensures legal compliance and performs regular data audits.

substeps.text: Consent forms clearly outline the purpose, scope, duration, and legal basis for data processing with airlines, hotels, visa agents, insurance providers, and government authorities.
Forms use plain language and are available in multiple regional languages.
Rights such as withdrawal, rectification, erasure, data portability, and complaint lodging are clearly stated.
Separate consent options are provided for essential services, marketing, profiling, data sharing, and loyalty programs.
Information on data retention, cross-border transfers, and automated decisions is included.
Consent is collected through online portals, mobile apps, office visits, calls, emails, and partner platforms.

Each consent is captured with detailed metadata including associated timestamp, IP address (for digital consents), staff member details (for offline consents), specific services being consented to, and version of consent form used, all stored securely to maintain a comprehensive and legally compliant audit trail.
We implement progressive consent mechanisms where customers can provide initial basic consent for essential services and later provide additional consent for enhanced services as needed.
All consent channels are integrated with our central consent management system to ensure consistency and avoid duplication of consent requests.
We provide confirmation mechanisms across all channels, including SMS confirmations, email receipts, and printed acknowledgments for offline consents.
Consent is tracked in an integrated system connected to booking, CRM, and customer databases.

Sophisticated role-based access controls with multi-level authorization are implemented to strictly restrict who can view, modify, or process consent records, ensuring data integrity, preventing unauthorized changes, and maintaining full compliance with stringent regulatory standards and industry best practices.
We maintain detailed consent audit logs tracking all access, modifications, and processing activities related to customer consent data.
The system includes automated consent validation checks to ensure all data processing activities are properly authorized before execution.
We implement systematic, scheduled reviews of all consent records on quarterly, semi-annual, and annual basis.

Customers are proactively notified through multiple channels (email, SMS, phone calls, and postal mail where necessary) of any significant changes in our data practices, policy updates, or regulatory changes that may affect their consent, and are given clear options to renew, modify, or update their consent accordingly with full transparency.
We maintain comprehensive records of all consent renewal activities, including customer responses, non-responses, and any follow-up actions taken.
Automated systems monitor consent expiry dates and trigger renewal processes in advance to ensure continuous compliance.
We provide customers with detailed summaries of their current consent status and easy options to modify their preferences at any time.
Consent withdrawal options include self-service online, email, phone, or written requests.
Requests are processed within regulatory timelines with documented records and confirmation.
Separate procedures exist for marketing, data sharing, and profiling withdrawals.
Legal retention obligations are explained.
Partial withdrawal is supported for specific purposes.
We proactively educate our customers through comprehensive, regular communication including detailed email updates.
Dedicated, well-trained customer support channels are available during extended business hours to address any questions, concerns.
We publish annual transparency reports detailing our data processing activities, consent management statistics, and privacy enhancement initiatives.
We maintain comprehensive compliance dashboards providing real-time visibility into consent management performance, regulatory compliance status, and audit findings.
Regular training and competency assessments are conducted for all staff involved in consent management activities.
We engage with external legal experts and privacy consultants to ensure our consent practices remain current with evolving legal requirements.

sections.title: Operational Process for Consulting and Informing Stakeholders

substeps.text: We provide detailed, clear, accessible, and regularly updated information to our customers regarding our comprehensive travel data handling practices through multiple communication channels including our company website with dedicated privacy sections, direct email communications with personalized content, detailed booking confirmations with privacy information, and personalized travel consultations with privacy discussions.
We disclose the specific travel data collected (e.g., passport, financials, preferences) and its use (e.g., bookings, insurance, personalization).
All communications are available in multiple languages and formats to ensure accessibility for customers with different needs and preferences.

Comprehensive, detailed documentation is maintained and regularly updated that thoroughly outlines every aspect of our travel data management practices including data collection procedures, processing workflows, storage security measures, sharing protocols, and disposal processes.
Documentation is accessible in digital and print formats, with simplified explanations and diagrams.
Documentation includes detailed flowcharts and process diagrams to help customers understand how their data flows through our systems.

Recognizing that questions, concerns, or requests may arise regarding travel data handling, privacy practices, or data rights, we have established multiple dedicated, specialized customer support channels.

Our customer service teams receive comprehensive, ongoing training to provide prompt, accurate, detailed, and helpful responses to any inquiries regarding travel data processing, privacy rights, consent management, and data security.
Support channels include dedicated privacy phone lines, specialized email support, live chat with privacy experts, and in-person consultations at our offices.
We publish regular transparency reports and maintain proactive, clear communication about data practices.
Updates are shared through emails, newsletters, the website, and direct consultations.
We offer opportunities for stakeholders to engage, ask questions, and share feedback on our privacy practices.

We enforce comprehensive, stringent, multi-layered role-based access controls across all aspects of our travel operations, ensuring that access to sensitive customer travel data is granted only to specifically authorized personnel.
Our sophisticated IT systems are designed and continuously maintained to enforce these security controls rigorously and consistently.
These comprehensive security measures include the implementation of advanced encryption protocols for data transmission to travel partners and government systems.
We implement principle of least privilege access, ensuring employees have access only to the specific data required for their job functions.
Regular access reviews are conducted to identify and remove unnecessary access permissions and to ensure compliance with data protection policies.
All access activities are logged and monitored through advanced security information and event management (SIEM) systems.

We place paramount importance on the physical security of our office-based data storage facilities, customer service areas, and all locations where sensitive travel information is stored, processed, or accessed, implementing multiple layers of physical security controls and monitoring systems.

Areas where confidential travel information is stored, including secure filing cabinets for physical documents, dedicated server rooms and IT equipment areas, customer service workstations, meeting rooms where customer data is discussed, and administrative areas with access to customer files, are strictly accessible only to specifically authorized personnel with verified identity and legitimate business need.

Comprehensive physical security measures include sophisticated access card systems with individual tracking and logging, advanced surveillance systems with 24/7 monitoring and recording, high-security locked filing cabinets.
Physical security incidents are immediately investigated and reported through established procedures.
All employees undergo regular, mandatory data protection training tailored to the travel industry, including handling of sensitive documents like passports, visa details, and financial data.
Staff are evaluated through annual assessments, refresher sessions, and specialized training for high-risk roles.
Continuous monitoring tools track access behaviour and flag suspicious activity, with clear escalation protocols for potential breaches.

sections.title: Internal Controls to Restrict Data Access

substeps.text: Our IT infrastructure includes multi-layered security such as multi-factor authentication and role-based access controls with detailed permission matrices for all platforms.
These controls ensure only authorized personnel with job-specific roles access sensitive travel data, with full logging, monitoring, audits, and periodic permission reviews.
Frequent updates, patches, vulnerability scans, penetration testing, and audits reinforce security and ensure continuous protection of customer management systems.
We deploy DLP systems to detect and prevent unauthorized transfers or downloads of sensitive data across all travel platforms and databases.
Office-based data areas, IT rooms, and service zones are protected using advanced multi-factor access controls to block unauthorized physical entry.
Entry requires verified credentials via access cards, biometric scans, CCTV monitoring, visitor escort logs, and is documented through electronic tracking.
Only authorized staff with validated business need can enter sensitive areas, maintaining maximum security for all customer data and systems.
Access logs are reviewed regularly to identify abnormal or unauthorized attempts and improve control over data-sensitive locations.
Internal and external audits occur monthly, quarterly, and annually to ensure access control effectiveness and identify improvement opportunities in data handling.
These audits proactively reveal security gaps, system weaknesses, or compliance risks, allowing timely updates to our travel data procedures.

blocks.text: Digital Storage: Records are stored on encrypted servers with role-based access controls.
