Annual Review: The retention policy is reviewed every year to ensure alignment with evolving legal and business needs.
Compliance Assurance: Practices are regularly audited to ensure compliance with Indian data protection and labor laws.
We use an integrated CRM, booking, and document management system to maintain detailed travel data records.
Access logs, customer consent forms (with version control), booking records, and compliance documents are systematically tracked and updated.
Real-time updates ensure data accuracy, with encrypted daily backups, weekly full backups, monthly offsite archiving, and quarterly disaster recovery tests.
Records are retained per legal, regulatory, tax, and internal policy requirements, with automated disposal for expired data.
The system enables efficient audits, ensures transparency in data handling, supports service delivery, and guarantees compliance across travel operations.
Internal audits are conducted monthly and quarterly; certified external reviews take place annually to assess compliance and identify improvements.
Employee input is gathered via surveys, feedback programs, meetings, and formal reviews to improve data handling and security.
Audit outcomes are analyzed, prioritized, and used to update access controls, retention schedules, security protocols, and training.
Practices are continuously refined to stay compliant with travel industry regulations and data protection laws.
Benchmarking against industry peers helps us identify and apply best practices in data management and protection.

sops.title: Incident Response Plan (IRP) for Breaches of Confidential Information

blocks.text: Protecting confidential customer information—including personal travel details, payment data, identification documents, and related records—is critical to maintaining trust and regulatory compliance. This Incident Response Plan (IRP) defines the steps to be followed immediately upon detection of any suspected or confirmed breach of confidential information within our travel operations.

Detect and respond swiftly to breaches involving confidential data.
Contain and mitigate impact of data breaches.
Comply with legal and regulatory reporting requirements.
Communicate effectively internally and externally.
Prevent recurrence by addressing root causes and improving controls.
This IRP applies to all types of breaches involving confidential data, including but not limited to:

Unauthorized access, disclosure, or theft of customer travel records or payment information.
Loss or compromise of employee or third-party data related to travel services.
IT system intrusions, malware attacks, or insider threats affecting confidential data.

responsibilities: A cross-functional team responsible for managing incident response activities, including IT, Compliance, Legal, Communications, and Operations representatives.
Detects breaches, leads technical investigation, containment, and remediation.
Ensures regulatory requirements for breach notification and reporting are met.
Advises on legal obligations, communications, and potential liabilities.
Manages internal and external communications, including customer notifications if required.
Provide expertise on affected data and assist in impact assessment.
Immediately report suspected breaches or security incidents to IT Security Lead or Incident Response Team.

body.text: The Incident Response Plan (IRP) is activated under the following circumstances:

Unauthorized Access: If there is any indication or detection of unauthorized individuals accessing confidential data.
Data Leaks: If sensitive or classified information is inadvertently or maliciously exposed to unauthorized parties.
Malicious Activity: Detection of malware, phishing, or hacking attempts that compromise the integrity of confidential data.
Inconsistent Records: Unexplained discrepancies in data records or transaction logs that indicate potential breaches or fraud.
Reports of Suspicious Activity: Employees or external stakeholders report activities that could jeopardize the security of confidential information, including suspicious access or sharing patterns.
Third-Party Security Failure: When a third-party partner or service provider reports a breach of the data they are responsible for managing.
Unusual System Activity: Abnormal patterns or behaviors identified in system logs, indicating potential data theft, tampering, or loss.

narrative.text:
All employees and authorized users are trained and required to remain vigilant for any suspicious activity, abnormal system behavior, unauthorized data access, or any other signs indicating a potential breach of confidential information.
Upon identifying or suspecting a breach, personnel must promptly report the incident through the designated communication channels—such as the internal incident reporting portal, hotline, or direct communication with the IT Security Lead.
Incident reports should be as detailed as possible, including date and time of occurrence, nature and scope of the incident, systems or data involved, any immediate actions taken, and relevant contextual information to assist rapid assessment.

blocks.text:
The Incident Response Team will immediately classify the reported incident based on established criteria, including the sensitivity of the data involved, the number of affected records, and the potential impact on customers and business continuity.
Incident severity categories are defined as follows:
High Severity: Breaches affecting large volumes of sensitive customer information such as financial data or government-issued identification, with significant potential harm or regulatory consequences.
Medium Severity: Breaches involving a limited subset of data or internal records with moderate impact on operations or compliance.
Low Severity: Incidents involving minimal exposure or isolated events with negligible risk to customers or the organization.
The severity classification will guide the prioritization of response efforts and resource allocation to ensure swift containment and remediation.

steps.heading: Immediate Action by the First Person to Detect the Breach

body.text: The first employee or authorized user who detects or suspects a breach involving confidential information must take the following critical and immediate actions to ensure swift containment and preservation of evidence:

Do Not Ignore the Incident: Every suspicion or indication of a data breach, regardless of how minor or insignificant it may initially appear, must be treated with the highest level of urgency and seriousness. Prompt reporting and response are essential to mitigate potential damage.
Contain the Situation: Where feasible and without risking further damage, the employee should take proactive steps to limit the breach’s scope and prevent any additional unauthorized access or data leakage. Such actions include:
Disconnecting the affected devices or systems from the corporate network to halt any ongoing compromise or data exfiltration.
Securing user accounts by immediately locking access or forcing password resets to block unauthorized users.
Stopping any ongoing transmissions or processes that may be leaking confidential data.
Notify the Incident Response Team (IRT) Without Delay: The breach must be reported instantly through designated company communication channels—whether via a dedicated incident reporting hotline, secure email, or an internal incident management system—to ensure that the Incident Response Team can mobilize and coordinate an effective response immediately.
Record Initial Details Accurately: The person who detected the breach must document all relevant preliminary information to assist the investigation, including:
The exact date and time the breach was detected.
Specific systems, applications, or datasets potentially affected.
Any immediate containment actions taken.
Names of any involved or impacted individuals or departments.
Do Not Alter the Evidence: It is imperative to avoid making any unauthorized changes to affected systems, data files, or logs. Preserving the integrity of all digital and physical evidence is essential to support forensic investigation and legal compliance.

The IRT will immediately take necessary actions to contain the breach, such as isolating affected systems or networks, suspending compromised user accounts, and blocking unauthorized access points to prevent further data loss.
All potentially compromised devices, logs, and evidence will be preserved in a secure manner, ensuring the integrity of data for forensic analysis without alteration or destruction.
Initial containment activities will be carefully documented to support ongoing investigation and regulatory compliance.

A comprehensive technical investigation will be conducted by IT Security to determine the root cause of the breach, attack vectors utilized, and the full scope of impacted systems and data.
The investigation will identify all records and customers potentially affected by the breach and assess the risk of harm, including identity theft, financial fraud, or reputational damage.
Coordination with external cybersecurity experts may be engaged if necessary to facilitate in-depth forensic analysis.

steps.heading: Notification and Reporting

body.text:
The Compliance Officer, in consultation with Legal Counsel, will ensure that all required notifications to regulatory authorities are submitted within applicable statutory deadlines, including detailed breach reports as mandated by law.
Affected customers will be notified promptly via appropriate communication channels (email, letter, phone) with clear, honest, and reassuring information regarding the nature of the breach, potential risks, recommended protective measures, and available support resources such as credit monitoring services.
Internal management and key stakeholders will receive timely updates regarding the status of the incident and response efforts.
All communication records and timelines will be meticulously maintained.

steps.responsible: Compliance Officer, in consultation with Legal Counsel

body.text:
The IT Security team will undertake corrective measures to remove malicious software, close exploited vulnerabilities, strengthen security controls, and apply necessary patches or configuration changes.
Systems affected by the breach will be restored from verified clean backups where applicable to ensure operational stability.
Enhanced monitoring and detection mechanisms will be implemented to observe for any signs of persistent threats or attempted recurrence.
Verification of full system recovery and security validation will be completed before resuming normal operations.

A formal post-incident review meeting will be convened involving all relevant stakeholders to evaluate the overall response effectiveness, challenges encountered, and lessons learned.
Root cause analysis will be finalized, and a detailed incident report will be prepared, including timelines, technical findings, impact assessments, and recommendations.
The IRP and related policies, procedures, and training materials will be updated based on the findings to strengthen the organization’s resilience against future breaches.
Any disciplinary or corrective actions for personnel involved will be handled per company policy.

blocks.text:
All communication related to the incident—whether internal updates, customer notifications, or media statements—will follow pre-approved templates and messages developed in coordination with Legal and Compliance teams to ensure clarity, consistency, and compliance with privacy laws.
Communications will be conducted transparently and professionally, aiming to maintain customer confidence and protect the company’s reputation.
Only authorized spokespeople will engage with external parties, including regulatory agencies and media.

Regular and comprehensive training programs will be conducted for all employees to enhance awareness of data protection responsibilities, signs of potential breaches, and the correct procedures for reporting incidents.
The Incident Response Team will participate in periodic simulation exercises and tabletop scenarios to practice response coordination and improve overall preparedness.
Training effectiveness will be measured and updated regularly to reflect evolving threats and regulatory changes.

Every incident will be fully documented in an incident management system, including detection details, investigation findings, containment actions, communications, and recovery processes.
Incident records will be securely stored, access-controlled, and retained for periods consistent with legal, regulatory, and company policy requirements.
Documentation will be made available for audit and regulatory review as required.

sops.title: Sensitive Transaction Approval and Management Protocol

blocks.text: At RIYA TRAVEL AND TOURS (INDIA) PVT LTD (GROUP), we are firmly committed to managing all sensitive transactions with the highest degree of integrity, transparency, and accountability. This SOP defines a clear, streamlined process for initiating, reviewing, and approving transactions that require special oversight. Our approach ensures compliance with internal policies and regulatory mandates while safeguarding the company’s reputation, financial interests, and ethical standards.

To establish a well-documented, standardized procedure for reporting and obtaining approvals for sensitive transactions.
To maintain the integrity of all transactions, preventing any undue influence, favoritism, or preferential treatment.
To create an efficient, structured approval workflow that minimizes unnecessary delays while ensuring rigorous review and compliance.
To achieve consistency by standardizing approval criteria and documentation across all departments and units.

This SOP applies universally across RIYA TRAVEL AND TOURS (INDIA) PVT LTD (GROUP) to all employees, managers, and departments involved in initiating, processing, or approving sensitive transactions. It encompasses dealings with external stakeholders, non-standard exchanges such as gifts, discounts, or high-value concessions, and transactions meeting or exceeding predefined financial or operational thresholds. This also includes transactions that could potentially affect procurement fairness or be perceived as conflicts of interest or favoritism.

responsibilities: Oversees overall transaction strategy, ensures compliance with company policies, reviews and approves high-tier transactions, and monitors adherence across the organization.
Supervises implementation of transaction protocols, coordinates review processes, supports escalation procedures, and facilitates internal audits related to sensitive transactions.
Performs financial analysis and risk assessments of transactions; reviews proposals for compliance with financial controls and documents approvals.
Evaluates vendor-related transactions to ensure fair evaluation and due diligence; secures necessary sign-offs within procurement processes.
Provides final oversight on the financial integrity of transactions, validating compliance with monetary thresholds, reviewing transaction records, and coordinating final approvals.
Ensures ethical management of employee-related and internal transactions, oversees conflict of interest disclosures, and guarantees transparency.

blocks.text: The following roles bear specific responsibilities to ensure effective management and control of sensitive transactions:
The approval of sensitive transactions follows a structured multi-step process:

body.text: The transaction initiator must complete a detailed proposal form, outlining the transaction’s description, rationale, expected outcomes, estimated financial impact, risk assessments, and relevant supporting documents such as contracts or vendor proposals.

Department heads review the submitted proposal to assess alignment with departmental objectives and risk thresholds. They provide recommendations and forward the proposal to Finance and Legal teams for further analysis.

The Finance and Legal teams conduct comprehensive financial assessments, verify legal compliance, and evaluate risks to ensure no external influence or favoritism compromises the transaction’s integrity.
Based on the transaction’s value and risk level, proposals are escalated to the appropriate level of senior management or the Board for final approval. Each approval step is fully documented.

Upon receiving all necessary approvals, the transaction is formally authorized for execution. The responsible department completes the transaction and archives all documentation, including approvals and due diligence records.

blocks.text: Transactions may involve cash, in-kind contributions, or non-monetary favors. In-kind or service-related transactions with significant market value or reputational impact undergo special review and may require senior-level approval.

Risk assessments consider financial impact, legal and regulatory compliance, potential conflicts of interest, and involvement of external stakeholders. Any indication of conflict or significant external influence triggers additional scrutiny and independent oversight.

Before engaging with any external stakeholder, RIYA TRAVEL AND TOURS conducts due diligence to evaluate their background, reputation, and any conflicts of interest. All interactions, negotiations, and communications are thoroughly documented and attached to the transaction record.

sections.title: Conflict of Interest and Favor Reporting

blocks.text: Employees are required to disclose any gifts, benefits, or preferential treatment offered by external parties that could influence transaction outcomes. Such instances must be promptly reported to the Compliance Officer using designated forms. The Compliance Officer, together with senior management, evaluates these reports to ensure transaction integrity. Decisions and corrective actions are documented appropriately.

Our ERP and document management systems maintain real-time, comprehensive logs of all sensitive transactions. These include transaction values, involved stakeholders, approval statuses, and related communications. All records are securely backed up monthly and archived for audit readiness and compliance verification.

Regular internal audits and annual external reviews assess the effectiveness of our sensitive transaction management protocols. Feedback from employees and audit findings guide updates to procedures, approval thresholds, and control mechanisms. This ongoing refinement ensures our practices remain aligned with evolving regulations, industry best practices, and organizational objectives.

RIYA TRAVEL AND TOURS ensures that every sensitive transaction complies with applicable laws, regulations, and internal policies. We monitor regulatory developments and promptly update this SOP accordingly. Our proactive risk management identifies potential issues early, enabling effective mitigation strategies. We uphold ethical business practices through transparency, regular reviews, and by adopting advanced technologies to optimize approval workflows. Benchmarking against industry leaders supports sustainable growth and governance excellence.

This SOP defines the procedures for conducting thorough due diligence to evaluate and monitor the ethical compliance of our suppliers, safeguarding our company’s reputation and aligning our supply chain with our sustainability goals.

To establish a structured process for assessing third-party suppliers on their compliance with ESG criteria.
To mitigate risks related to unethical practices, non-compliance with regulations, and social or environmental harm.
To promote transparency, accountability, and continuous improvement within our supply chain.

To systematically evaluate the company's adherence to internal policies, regulatory requirements, and industry best practices.

This SOP establishes the sustainable procurement practices at Riya Travel and Tours (India) Pvt Ltd (Group), ensuring procurement decisions integrate environmental stewardship, ethical governance, and social responsibility. It mandates adherence to our Supplier Code of Conduct, reflecting our commitment to sustainable and responsible supply chain management within the travel and tourism sector.

This procedure applies to procurement of all goods and services including travel-related services, technology, office supplies, third-party vendors, and consultants. It covers new and existing suppliers at all levels of the supply chain supporting our operations.

Integrate sustainability principles into procurement policies and daily purchasing activities.
Ensure all suppliers comply with Riya Travel and Tours’ Supplier Code of Conduct.
Promote environmental performance, fair labor practices, and ethical governance among suppliers.
Enhance supplier diversity, including engagement with women-owned, minority-led, and vulnerable-group enterprises.
Align procurement decisions with our long-term ESG (Environmental, Social, Governance) goals.

Supplier Code of Conduct Compliance: All suppliers must acknowledge and comply with our Supplier Code of Conduct, covering human rights, business ethics, environmental responsibility, and workplace safety.
Environmental Sustainability: Procurement prioritizes suppliers who demonstrate responsible practices such as reducing emissions, minimizing waste, and conserving resources relevant to the travel industry.
Social Accountability: Suppliers must ensure decent working conditions, fair wages, health and safety measures, and prohibition of child or forced labor.
Supplier Diversity: We actively promote engagement with diverse suppliers including women-owned, minority-owned, and other underrepresented groups. Preference is given to those registered with recognized certification bodies or associations for diversity.
Governance and Ethics: Procurement decisions are made free from favoritism, corruption, or conflicts of interest; suppliers must uphold high ethical standards.

narrative.text:
Pre-Qualification and ESG Screening: Suppliers disclose diversity ownership status during onboarding. Priority is given to vendors registered with recognized diversity organizations or local/national associations.
On-site Supplier Audits: For strategic or high-risk suppliers, scheduled on-site or virtual audits assess compliance with sustainability practices, occupational health and safety, diversity and inclusion, social and environmental standards, and our Supplier Code of Conduct.
Supplier Worker Feedback Surveys: Anonymous surveys gather feedback from supplier employees on working conditions, safety, grievance mechanisms, and fair treatment. Results guide assessment of supplier alignment with our Code of Conduct.
Annual Assessments: Existing suppliers undergo annual sustainability performance reviews using ESG KPIs, audit findings, and survey feedback. Non-compliant suppliers face warnings, corrective monitoring, or contract termination.
